newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle ends weak with cash, fund selling.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle ends weak with cash, fund selling.

text.p: Lower cash beef and cattle prices and fund liquidation knocked CME live cattle futures lower at the close, traders said.
Live cattle futures closed 1.025 cent per lb lower to unchanged with February pacing the setback at 64.325 cents, its lowest level since December 23.

Continued weakness in cash beef and feedlots selling their cattle $1 per cwt lower at $65 Tuesday weighed on live cattle futures. Feedlots accepted lower packer bids when it became apparent sliding beef prices would not allow packers to offer steady to higher bids, traders said.

"There was some hope that the weather would be bad enough to stiffen the backs of the cattle feeders and prevent them from selling cattle but that didn't happen. Beef is still a little bit on the sloppy side and apparently hasn't bottomed yet and that's contributing to the problem as well," said Tom Tippens, CEO of Professional Cattle Consultants Inc.

Weakness in cash also may be a function of producer concerns that there are still ample numbers of cattle eventually coming to market. Feedlots want to sell cattle before larger numbers become available later in the month, a scenario that is giving packers the advantage, Tippens added.
